input.question: Can someone explain what a mortgage is (LI5)?
input.ground_truth: A mortgage is simply a loan that a bank gives you so that you can buy a house. Most people don't have enough money on hand to pay the full price for a house so they will get a loan from the bank, called a mortgage, that is to be used strictly for the purchase of a house. The bank requires you to pay back a certain amount of the loan, with interest, every month just like any other loan. If you stop paying your mortgage the bank has the legal right to foreclose on your home, which means that they can force you to leave and sell the house to get their money back. Once you pay back your mortgage in full the bank no longer has any legal claim on your house.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Can someone explain what a mortgage is (LI5)?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Sure! Imagine you really, really want a big toy castle, but you don't have enough money to buy it right now. So, you ask the toy store if you can pay for the castle a little bit at a time, instead of all at once. The toy store says yes, but they want you to promise to pay them back over many years, and they also want you to give them something (like a picture of your piggy bank or a special promise) to make sure you will pay them back.

A **mortgage** is like that, but for a big house instead of a toy castle. You promise to pay the bank or a special company little by little every month, until you’ve paid for the whole house. The house is like your big toy, and the promise you make is very important!
